framework_detected: In medias res (8:57, Send hovered, model ≠ deck) rewinding into PAS. Fully executed as a structure: climax, '45 MINUTES EARLIER', then three escalating failures. The Solve leg arrives only at 46 s, so PAS is front-loaded on Agitate.
framework_recommended: In medias res into a compressed PAS. It is the right pick for an anxious finance/legal buyer whose pain is a deadline, but the agitate leg should end by ~30 s and a 1-2 s glimpse of the real diff should be teased inside the first 12 s, so the viewer knows relief is coming.

hook_alternatives.first_3s_visual: Real chatbot-style green check 'Done.' fills frame, then hard cut to the deck slide 4 still reading €71–73m, ringed red
hook_alternatives.line: 'Done' is the most expensive word in AI.
hook_alternatives.why: The film's whole thesis in one contradiction; legible sound-off, and the '≠' becomes the visual punchline instead of a static card.

hook_alternatives.first_3s_visual: Split frame: left, three files with €74.6m / €71–73m / €71–73m in red; right, the real Changes panel '10 of 10 reviewed', all €74.6m
hook_alternatives.line: One number. Three files. Ten places it lives.
hook_alternatives.why: Shows the real product proof in second 1, solving the 46 s wait for credibility, and uses the approved 10-of-10 truth.

hook_alternatives.first_3s_visual: Real footage: her finger over the trackpad, Send glowing, wall clock 8:57, VO silent; super 'Would you send this?'
hook_alternatives.line: Board in three minutes. Would you send this?
hook_alternatives.why: Makes the viewer the protagonist and the decision the hook; a human face and a real room stop the scroll better than a flat email UI.

issues.evidence: f_01 (0.0 s) and f_02 (2.5 s) are the same flat grey email illustration with floated cards and an 'ILLUSTRATION' tag; the promised real laptop cold open is not visible in either sampled frame, and nothing moves except the cursor reaching Send.
issues.suggested_action: Verify the 0–1.2 s laptop shot exists; if so lengthen it to ~2 s and make it the first frame (real room, her hand, screen glow) with the ≠ cards tracked above, then push into the email.

issues.evidence: The product first appears at 46 s (f_20, logo + 'See exactly what changed'); 0–46 s is all failure. For a 121 s ad the proof/roadmap window is 12–25 s.
issues.suggested_action: Insert a 1.5 s flash-forward around 10–12 s of the real Changes panel row 'Slide 4 title €71–73m → €74.6m' with no logo, so the viewer is promised the payoff; or cut one of the three 'Done' cycles.

issues.evidence: VO 'And the deck doesn't match the model' is concrete, but the on-screen cards are small, top-right, and compete with the large white email body; at feed size the ≠ reads as decoration.
issues.suggested_action: Make the two numbers the dominant element (60% of frame), dim the email body, and let the red '≠' snap in on a hit at 0.4 s.

issues.evidence: Opening clock reads 8:57, yet the flashback later shows 8:58 (f_17) before we return to the same email, so 'Forty-five minutes earlier' does not hold up for an attentive viewer.
issues.suggested_action: Set the cold-open clock to 8:59 or cap the montage clock at 8:56 so the loop closes cleanly.

issues.evidence: f_10 and f_13: the head-in-hands clip shows a black band across the top and down the right edge.
issues.suggested_action: Scale the clip to fill the frame (~112%) so the human reaction beat reads as cinema, not a mis-sized insert.

top_revision: Open on 2 s of the real laptop/her hand over Send with the two numbers dominating the frame, and plant a 1.5 s flash of the real 'Slide 4 title €71–73m → €74.6m' diff by ~12 s so the hook promises its payoff long before 46 s.
